checks.name: snr
checks.reason: The dip stands 58 times above the noise over 24 events.

checks.name: odd_even
checks.reason: Alternate dips have different depths (0.890% vs 0.552%, 4.6 sigma apart). A planet makes identical dips; two stars eclipsing each other usually do not, so the true period is likely 4.4372 days.

checks.name: secondary_eclipse
checks.reason: Halfway round the orbit there is no significant dip, consistent with a planet.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: Depth 0.890% on a star 0.83 times the Sun's size gives 0.76 Jupiter radii (likely 0.65 to 0.90). That is within the size range of planets.

checks.name: transit_count
checks.reason: 24 separate dips line up on the same period.

checks.name: depth_consistency
checks.reason: The dip has the same depth in every sector.

pixels.reason: the light lost in transit comes from the target (offset 0.4″ = 0.02 px, 0.8σ) and every Gaia neighbour able to mimic the dip is excluded by the centroid
